A large, swift stream or river can carry all sizes of particles, from clay to boulders. When the current slows down, its competence (how much it can carry) decreases and the stream deposits the largest particles in the streambed. If current velocity continues to decrease - as a flood wanes, for example - finer particles settle out on top of the large ones. Thus, a stream sorts its sediment according to size. A waning flood might deposit a layer of gravel, overlain by sand and finally topped by silt and clay. Streams also sort sediment in the downstream direction. Many mountain streams are choked with boulders and cobbles, but far downstream, their deltas are composed mainly of fine silt and clay. This downstream sorting is curious because stream velocity generally increases in the downstream direction. Competence increases with velocity, so a river should be able to transport larger particles than its tributaries carry. One explanation for downstream sorting is that abrasion wears away the boulders and cobbles to sand and silt as the sediment moves downstream over the years. Thus, only the fine sediment reaches the lower parts of most rivers.

A stream deposits its sediment in three environments: Alluvial fans and deltas form where stream gradient (angle of incline) suddenly decreases as a stream enters a flat plain, a lake, or the sea; floodplain deposits accumulate on a floodplain adjacent to the stream channel; and channel deposits form in the stream channel itself. Bars, which are elongated mounds of sediment, are transient features that form in the stream channel and on the banks. They commonly form in one year and erode the next. Rivers used for commercial navigation must be recharted frequently because bars shift from year to year. Imagine a winding stream. The water on the outside of the curve moves faster than the water on the inside. The stream erodes its outside bank because the current’s inertia drives it into the outside bank. At the same time, the slower water on the inside point of the bend deposits sediment, forming a point bar. A mid-channel bar is a sandy and gravelly deposit that forms in the middle of a stream channel.

Most streams flow in a single channel. In contrast, a braided stream flows in many shallow, interconnecting channels. A braided stream forms where more sediment is supplied to a stream than it can carry. The stream dumps the excess sediment, forming mid-channel bars. The bars gradually fill a channel, forcing the stream to overflow its banks and erode new channels. As a result, a braided stream flows simultaneously in several channels and shifts back and forth across its floodplain. Braided streams are common in both deserts and glacial environments because both produce abundant sediment. A desert yields large amounts of sediment because it has little or no vegetation to prevent erosion. Glaciers grind bedrock into fine sediment, which is carried by streams flowing from the melting ice. If a steep mountain stream flows onto a flat plain, its gradient and velocity decrease sharply. As a result, it deposits most of its sediment in a fan-shaped mound called an alluvial fan. Alluvial fans are common in many arid and semiarid mountainous regions.

A stream also slows abruptly where it enters the still water of a lake or ocean. The sediment settles out to form a nearly flat landform called a delta. Part of the delta lies above water level, and the remainder lies slightly below water level. Deltas are commonly fan-shaped, resembling the Greek letter “delta” (Δ). Both deltas and alluvial fans change rapidly. Sediment fills channels (waterways), which are then abandoned while new channels develop as in a braided stream. As a result, a stream feeding a delta or fan splits into many channels called distributaries. A large delta may spread out in this manner until it covers thousands of square kilometers. Most fans, however, are much smaller, covering a fraction of a square kilometer to a few square kilometers. The Mississippi River has flowed through seven different delta channels during the past 5,000 to 6,000 years. But in recent years, engineers have built great systems of levees (retaining walls) in attempts to stabilize the channels.

In the archaeological record of the Natufian period, from about 12,500 to 10,200 years ago, in the part of the Middle East known as the Levant―roughly east of the Mediterranean and north of the Arabian Peninsula―we see clear evidence of agricultural origins. The stone tools of the Natufians included many sickle-shaped cutting blades that show a pattern of wear characteristic of cereal harvesting. Also, querns (hand mills) and other stone tools used for processing grain occur in abundance at Natufian sites, and many such tools show signs of long, intensive use . Along with the sickle blades are many grinding stones, primarily mortars and pestles of limestone or basalt. There is also evidence that these heavy grinding stones were transported over long distances, more than 30 kilometers in some cases, and this is not something known to have been done by people of preceding periods. Fishhooks and weights for sinking fishing nets attest to the growing importance of fish in the diet in some areas. Stone vessels indicate an increased need for containers, but there is no evidence of Natufian clay working or pottery. Studies of the teeth of Natufians also strongly suggest that these people specialized in collecting cereals and may have been cultivating them and in the process of domesticating them, but they were also still hunter-foragers who intensively hunted gazelle and deer in more lush areas and wild goats and equids in more arid zones.

The Natufians had a different settlement pattern from that of their predecessors. Some of their base camps were far larger (over 1,000 square meters) than any of those belonging to earlier periods, and they may have lived in some of these camps for half the year or even more. In some of the camps, people made foundations and other architectural elements out of limestone blocks. Trade in shell, obsidian, and other commodities seems to have been on the rise, and anthropologists suspect that the exchange of perishables (such as skins, foodstuffs) and salt was also on the increase. With the growing importance of wild cereals in the diet, salt probably became for the first time a near necessity: people who eat a lot of meat get many essential salts from this diet, but diets based on cereals can be deficient in salts. Salt was probably also important as a food preservative in early villages.

As always, there is more to a major cultural change than simply a shift in economics. The Natufians made (and presumably wore) beads and pendants in many materials, including gemstones and marine shells that had to be imported, and it is possible that this ornamentation actually reflects a growing sense of ethnic identity and perhaps some differences in personal and group status. Cleverly carved figurines of animals, women, and other subjects occur in many sites, and Natufian period cave paintings have been found in Anatolia, Syria, and Iran. More than 400 Natufian burials have been found, most of them simple graves set in house floors. As archaeologist Belfer-Cohen notes, these burials may reflect an ancestor cult and a growing sense of community emotional ties and attachment to a particular place, and toward the end of the Natufian period, people in this area were making a strict separation between living quarters and burial grounds. In contrast with the Pleistocene cultures of the Levant, Natufian culture appears to have experienced considerable social change.

The question of why the Natufians differed from their predecessors in these and other ways and why they made these first steps toward farming as a way of life remains unclear. There were climate changes, of course, and growing aridity and rising population densities may have forced them to intensify the exploitation of cereals, which in turn might have stimulated the development of sickles and other tools and the permanent communities that make agriculture efficient. But precisely how these factors interacted with others at play is poorly understood.

At the end of the Pleistocene (around 10,000 B.C.), the technologies of food production may have already been employed on the fringes of the rain forests of western and central Africa, where the common use of such root plants as the African yam led people to recognize the advantages of growing their own food. The yam can easily be resprouted if the top is replanted. This primitive form of “vegeculture” (cultivation of root and tree crops) may have been the economic tradition onto which the cultivation of summer rainfall cereal crops was grafted as it came into use south of the grassland areas on the Sahara’s southern borders.

As the Sahara dried up after 5000 B.C., pastoral peoples (cattle herders) moved southward along major watercourses into the savanna belt of West Africa and the Sudan. By 3000 B.C., just as ancient Egyptian civilization was coming into being along the Nile, they had settled in the heart of the East African highlands far to the south. The East African highlands are ideal cattle country and the home today of such famous cattle-herding peoples as the Masai. The highlands were inhabited by hunter-gatherers living around mountains near the plains until about 3300 B.C., when the first cattle herders appeared. These cattle people may have moved between fixed settlements during the wet and dry seasons, living off hunting in the dry months and their own livestock and agriculture during the rains.

As was the case elsewhere, cattle were demanding animals in Africa. They required water at least every 24 hours and large tracts of grazing grass if herds of any size were to be maintained. The secret was the careful selection of grazing land, especially in environments where seasonal rainfall led to marked differences in graze quality throughout the year. Even modest cattle herds required plenty of land and considerable mobility. To acquire such land often required moving herds considerable distances, even from summer to winter pastures. At the same time, the cattle owners had to graze their stock in tsetse-fly-free areas. The only protection against human and animal sleeping sickness, a disease carried by the tsetse fly, was to avoid settling or farming such areas- a constraint severely limiting the movements of cattle-owning farmers in eastern and central Africa. As a result, small cattle herds spread south rapidly in areas where they could be grazed. Long before cereal agriculture took hold far south of the Sahara, some hunter-gatherer groups in the savanna woodlands of eastern and southern Africa may have acquired cattle, and perhaps other domesticated animals, by gift exchange or through raids on herding neighbors.

Contrary to popular belief, there is no such phenomenon as “pure” pastoralists, a society that subsists on its herds alone. The Saharan herders who moved southward to escape drought were almost certainly also cultivating sorghum, millet, and other tropical rainfall crops. By 1500 B.C., cereal agriculture was widespread throughout the savanna belt south of the Sahara. Small farming communities dotted the grasslands and forest margins of eastern West Africa, all of them depending on what is called shifting agriculture. This form of agriculture involved clearing woodland, burning the felled brush over the cleared plot, mixing the ash into the soil, and then cultivating the prepared fields. After a few years, the soil was exhausted, so the farmer moved on, exploiting new woodland and leaving the abandoned fields to lie fallow. Shifting agriculture, often called slash-and-burn, was highly adaptive for savanna farmers without plows, for it allowed cereal farming with the minimal expenditure of energy.

The process of clearance and burning may have seemed haphazard to the uninformed eye, but it was not. Except in favored areas, such as regularly inundated floodplains, tropical Africa’s soils were of only moderate to low fertility. The art of farming was careful soil selection, that is, knowing which soils were light and easily cultivable, could be readily turned with small hoes, and would maintain their fertility over several years` planting, for cereal crops rapidly remove nitrogen and other nutrients from the soil. Once it had taken hold, slash-and-burn agriculture expanded its frontiers rapidly as village after village took up new lands, moving forward so rapidly that one expert has estimated it took a mere two centuries to cover 2,000 kilometers from eastern to southern Africa.

atheism/ˈeɪθiɪzəm/n.无神论Atheism is a philosophical or religious position that rejects the belief in the existence of gods or any supernatural deities / His atheism caused some conflict with his religious family.

invalid/ˈɪnvəlɪd/n.病人，伤残人An invalid is someone who needs to be cared for because they have an illness or disability / After the accident, he became an invalid and needed constant care / She had been a delicate child and her parents had treated her as an invalid

diagnose/ˈdaɪəɡnoʊz/v.诊断，判断The doctor was able to diagnose the disease as malaria
diagnosis/ˌdaɪəɡˈnoʊsɪs/n.诊断The doctor’s diagnosis was that she had a mild form of the flu
remedy/ˈrɛmɪdi/n.治疗方法Herbal teas can be a good remedy for common colds / There are many different kinds of natural remedies to help overcome winter infections.
prescription/prɪˈskrɪpʃən/n.处方，药方The doctor gave her a prescription for antibiotics
dissect/daɪˈsɛkt/v.解剖In biology class, we had to dissect a frog
sterile/ˈstɛrəl/adj.无菌的，消过毒的It’s important to use sterile equipment in surgeries / sterile water
anatomy/əˈnætəmi/n.解剖学We learned about the human heart in anatomy class
healthful/ˈhɛlθfʊl/adj.有益健康的Eating a balanced diet is healthful / Does the college cafeteria provide a healthful diet
hygiene/ˈhaɪdʒiːn/n.卫生Good personal hygiene can prevent many diseases.
sanitation/ˌsænɪˈteɪʃən/n.公共卫生The city has made efforts to improve sanitation in poor neighborhoods / disease resulting from poor sanitation

malnourished/mælˈnʌrɪʃt/adj.营养不良的Malnourished children often suffer from stunted growth
nutrition/nuːˈtrɪʃən/n.营养Good nutrition is essential for maintaining health
spiritual/ˈspɪrɪtʃuəl/adj.精神的，心灵的Yoga is often seen as both a physical and spiritual practice / a spiritual experience

inoculation/ɪˌnɒkjʊˈleɪʃən/n.接种，疫苗接种Inoculation against the disease is highly recommended / This may eventually lead to routine inoculation of children

carbon/ˈkɑːrbən/n.碳Carbon is a non-metallic element found in all organic life
nitrogen/ˈnaɪtrədʒən/n.氮The tanker was carrying liquid nitrogen
oxygen/ˈɑːksɪdʒən/n.氧Oxygen is essential for most life forms on Earth.
fluorine/ˈflʊəriːn/n.氟Fluorine is a highly reactive, pale yellow gas.
neon/ˈniːɒn/n.氖Neon is a noble gas used in neon lights.
sodium/ˈsoʊdiəm/n.钠Sodium is a soft, reactive metal used in many salts
magnesium/mægˈniːziəm/n.镁，镁元素Magnesium is a light, silvery-white metal
aluminum/əˈluːmɪnəm/n.铝Aluminum is a lightweight, ductile metal used in many industries.
silicon/ˈsɪlɪkɒn/n.硅Silicon is commonly used in the semiconductor industry
phosphorus/ˈfɑːsfərəs/n.磷Phosphorus is a highly-reactive, nonmetallic element
sulfur/ˈsʌlfər/n.硫Sulfur is a yellow chemical element used in the production of sulfuric acid.
chlorine/ˈklɔːriːn/n.氯Chlorine is a yellow-green gas at room temperature.
argon/ˈɑːrgɒn/n.氩Argon is a colorless, odorless noble gas used in light bulbs.
potassium/pəˈtæsiəm/n.钾Potassium is a soft, silvery-white metal, vital for living organisms.
calcium/ˈkælsiəm/n.钙Calcium is important for healthy bones and teeth.
copper/ˈkɑːpər/n.铜Copper is a useful metal for conducting electricity
lead/lɛd/n.铅Lead is a heavy, soft, malleable metal.
mercury/ˈmɜːrkjʊri/n.水银，汞Mercury is a liquid metal used in many thermometers
nickel/ˈnɪkəl/n.镍Nickel is a silver-white metal used in various alloys
platinum/ˈplætɪnəm/n.铂，白金Platinum is a precious metal that is more valuable than gold
silver/ˈsɪlvər/n.银Silver is a shiny, white metal often used for jewelry.
tin/tɪn/n.锡Tin is a soft, silvery-white metal used for coating steel
zinc/zɪŋk/n.锌Zinc is a useful metal in the production of batteries
caustic/ˈkɔːstɪk/adj.腐蚀性的Caustic chemicals can burn or corrode material surfaces / Remember that this is caustic, use gloves or a spoon
erosion/ɪˈroʊʒən/n.侵蚀，腐蚀Soil erosion is a common environmental concern
corrode/kəˈroʊd/v.腐蚀Salt water can corrode metal over time
rot/rɑːt/v./n.腐烂If you don’t preserve food properly, it will rot
rotten/ˈrɑːtn/adj.腐烂的The apple is rotten and not fit for consumption
decay/dɪˈkeɪ/v./n.腐烂The smell of death and decay hung over the town
decomposition/ˌdiːkɒmpəˈzɪʃən/n.分解，腐烂Decomposition of organic matter provides nutrients for plants
stale/steɪl/adj.(食物) 不新鲜的，变味的Stale bread is hard and not suitable for eating
rust/rʌst/v./n.生锈Iron can rust if exposed to moisture and oxygen
silica/ˈsɪlɪkə/n.二氧化硅Silica is a common component in sand and quartz
crystal/ˈkrɪstl/n.水晶，晶体Salt crystals are commonly used in chemistry experiments
gasoline/ˈgæsəliːn/n.汽油Gasoline is a common fuel used in most cars
methane/ˈmeθeɪn/n.甲烷，沼气Methane is a common greenhouse gas
hydrocarbon/ˌhaɪdrəʊˈkɑːrbən/n.烃，碳氢化合物Hydrocarbons are the main components of petroleum and natural gas
petroleum/pəˈtroʊliəm/n.石油Petroleum is used to make gasoline and other fuels
plastic/ˈplæstɪk/n.塑料Plastic is used in a variety of products, from bottles to toys
intermediary/ˌɪntərˈmiːdiːeri/n.中间人An intermediary substance facilitates a chemical reaction / She wanted him to act as an intermediary in the dispute with Moscow.
catalysis/kəˈtælɪsɪs/n.催化作用Catalysis speeds up a chemical reaction
catalyst/ˈkætəlɪst/n.催化剂Enzymes often act as biological catalysts
adhesive/ədˈhiːsɪv/n.粘合剂Glue is a common type of adhesive
scorch/skɔːrtʃ/v./n.烧焦/枯萎The leaves are inclined to scorch in hot sunshine
bleach/bliːtʃ/v./n.漂白You can bleach your clothes to remove stains
tint/tɪnt/v./n.色彩，色泽You can tint windows to reduce sunlight
dye/daɪ/v./n.染色，染料You can dye fabric to change its color
biochemistry/ˌbaɪoʊˈkemɪstri/n.生物化学Biochemistry is the study of chemical processes in living organisms
alchemy/ˈælkəmi/n.炼金术Alchemy is a historical predecessor to modern chemistry
ion/ˈaɪɒn/n.离子Ions are atoms or molecules with a net electric charge
molecule/ˈmɒlɪkjuːl/n.分子A molecule of water consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
solubility/ˌsɒljʊˈbɪlɪti/n.溶解性The solubility of a substance refers to its ability to dissolve in a solvent
solution/səˈluːʃn/n.溶液A salt solution is made by dissolving salt in water
solvent/ˈsɑːlvənt/n.溶剂A solvent is a liquid that can dissolve other substances / Water is a common solvent used in many chemical reactions
solute/ˈsɑːljuːt/n.溶质solvent + solute = solution
dissolve/dɪˈzɑːlv/v.溶解Sugar dissolves quickly in hot water
impurity/ɪmˈpjʊrəti/n.杂质Impurities in metals can weaken their strength
compound/ˈkɒmpaʊnd/n.化合物Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen
substance/ˈsʌbstəns/n.物质There’s absolutely no regulation of cigarettes to make sure that they don’t include poisonous substances
particle/ˈpɑːrtɪkl/n.粒子，颗粒Dust particles are very small and often not visible to the eye
explosive/ɪkˈsploʊsɪv/adj./n.爆炸性的/爆炸物an explosive device / The car had been rigged with about 300 lbs of explosive
explode/ɪkˈsploʊd/v.爆炸Gasoline can explode under certain conditions
blast/blæst/v./n.爆炸/一阵250 people were killed in the blast / A blast of wind can blow leaves off trees
burning/ˈbɜːrnɪŋ/adj./n.燃烧The burning wood crackled in the fireplace
kindle/ˈkɪndl/v.点燃to kindle a fire/flame / The Second World War kindled his enthusiasm for politics
sear/sɪr/v.烤焦；轻煎Sear the meat on high heat to lock in the juices
neutralize/ˈnuːtrəˌlaɪz/v.中和，抵消Vinegar can neutralize the effect of baking soda in a solution
polymerization/ˌpɑːlɪˈmɛrɪˌzeɪʃən/n.聚合作用Polymerization is a process used in making plastics
synthetic/sɪnˈθɛtɪk/adj.合成的Synthetic materials are used to make a variety of products
hackneyed/ˈhækniːd/adj.老生常谈的/ 不新奇的Power corrupts and absolute power corrupts absolutely.That’s the old hackneyed phrase, but it’s true

entry.title: TOEFL｜Vocab Law
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Law 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
penal/ˈpiːnəl/adj.刑罚的Penal means relating to the punishment of criminals / penal code (刑法) / the penal system
illicit/ɪˈlɪsɪt/adj.非法的illicit drugs / illicit trade
unruly/ʌnˈruːli/adj.难管教的difficult to control or manage / an unruly class / unruly behaviour / When you start meditating, you will notice how unruly the mind is
illegitimate/ˌɪlɪˈdʒɪtɪmət/adj.非法的/私生的illegitimate business / illegitimate child
default/dɪˈfɔːlt/n./v.违约to default on a loan / The corporation may be charged with default on its contract with the government.
violation/ˌvaɪəˈleɪʃən/n.违反，侵犯violation of the law / violation of rights
infringe/ɪnˈfrɪndʒ/v.侵犯，违反infringe a patent / infringe upon one’s rights
bound/baʊnd/adj./v.肯定会/约束bound to happen / bound by law
compulsory/kəmˈpʌlsəri/adj.强制性的/义务的English is a compulsory subject at this level / compulsory education/schooling
oblige/əˈblaɪdʒ/v.强制/迫使The storm got worse and worse. Finally, I was obliged to abandon the car and continue on foot.
obligatory/əˈblɪɡətɔːri/adj.(按法律)必须的It is obligatory for all employees to wear protective clothing / As part of the course requirements, students must fulfill the obligatory reading list / Following the regulations, providing proper safety gear is obligatory in this construction site
domineering/dəˈmiːnɪərɪŋ/adj.专横的/刚愎自用的trying to control other people without considering their opinions or feelings / Mick was stubborn and domineering with a very bad temper / She had to deal with a domineering mother-in-law who always interfered in her married life
mandatory/ˈmændətɔːri/adj.强制的/法定的the mandatory life sentence for murder / the mandatory retirement age of 65
licensed/ˈlaɪsənst/adj.持证的licensed driver / a licensed restaurant
heirship/ˈerʃɪp/n.继承权heirship disputes / Male or female can both have the heirship to the throne
jurisdiction/ˌdʒʊrɪsˈdɪkʃən/n.司法权，管辖权The British police have no jurisdiction over foreign bank accounts / The court determined that it had no jurisdiction over the dispute as the incident took place outside its territorial boundaries
arbitration/ˌɑːrbɪˈtreɪʃən/n.仲裁The judge said that arbitration was a fair and expeditious decision-making process / The contract between the two companies includes a clause mandating arbitration in case of any disputes
fine/faɪn/n./v.罚款to pay a fine / fine for speeding
confiscate/ˈkɒnfɪskeɪt/v.没收，充公The teacher threatened to confiscate their phones if they kept using them in class
convict/kənˈvɪkt/n./v.判罪In 1977 he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment
verdict/ˈvɜːrdɪkt/n.判决，裁定The jury returned a unanimous guilty verdict / Has the jury reached a verdict
indemnity/ɪnˈdɛmnɪti/n.赔偿，保障If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss / the software license agreement contained an indemnity clause protecting the developer from patent infringement claims
imprisonment/ɪmˈprɪzənmənt/n.监禁She was sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment / life imprisonment
invalidate/ɪnˈvælɪdeɪt/v.使无效，废除If something invalidates something such as a law, contract, or election, it causes it to be considered illegal
captivity/kæpˈtɪvɪti/n.囚禁，拘留Once more he felt the sense of captivity heavy upon him
trial/ˈtraɪəl/n.试验/审判clinical trial / trial for murder
detain/dɪˈteɪn/v.拘留，扣押detain a suspect
extenuate/ɪkˈstenjueɪt/v.减轻Nothing can extenuate his crime / The defendant’s lawyer tried to extenuate the client’s actions by highlighting their difficult upbringing and history of abuse
bar/bɑːr/n./v.阻挡/拦住Two police officers were barring her exit / We found our way barred by rocks
empower/ɪmˈpaʊər/v.使有能力You must delegate effectively and empower people to carry out their roles with your fullsupport
plea/pliː/n.（向法庭提供的）理由He was charged with murder, but got off on a plea of insanity
oath/əʊθ/n.宣誓，誓言take an oath / oath of office
pledge/plɛdʒ/n./v.誓言In the treaty both sides pledge to respect human rights
plaintiff/ˈpleɪntɪf/n.原告A plaintiff is a person who brings a legal case against someone in a court of law / Plaintiff is an antonym of defendant
plead/pliːd/v.辩护，恳求I was forced to plead for my child’s life / to plead guilty/not guilty
flee/fliː/v.逃走flee the country / flee from danger
defend/dɪˈfɛnd/v.为…辩护He has hired a lawyer to defend him against the allegation
proscribe/prəʊˈskraɪb/v.宣布禁止If something is proscribed by people in authority, the existence or the use of that thing is forbidden / They are proscribed by federal law from owning guns
abstain/əbˈsteɪn/v.弃权Three countries abstained in the vote
veto/ˈviːtoʊ/n./v.否决权/否决veto a bill / veto power (否决权)
stipulate/ˈstɪpjuleɪt/v.规定/ 明确要求PayPal policies stipulate that sellers must prove buyers received an item
testify/ˈtɛstɪfaɪ/v.(在法庭上) 作证He was summoned to testify before a grand jury
testimony/ˈtɛstɪmoʊni/n.证词His testimony was an important element of the prosecution’s case.
justify/ˈdʒʌstɪfaɪ/v.证明…是正当的No argument can justify a war
substantiate/səbˈstænʃieɪt/v.证实There is little scientific evidence to substantiate the claims
affirm/əˈfɜːrm/v.断言/证实If an event affirms something, it shows that it is true or exists / Everything I had accomplished seemed to affirm that opinion
allege/əˈledʒ/v.（未提出证据）断言If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it
assure/əˈʃʊr/v.保证，确保She’s perfectly safe, I can assure you
observe/əbˈzɜːrv/v.遵守/观察observe a law (遵守法律)
abide/əˈbaɪd/v.遵守abide by the rules
accuse/əˈkjuːz/v.指责，指控accuse someone of theft
impeach/ɪmˈpiːtʃ/v.弹劾，控告impeach a president
indictment/ɪnˈdaɪtmənt/n.控告，起诉An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime / The news of the indictment shocked the community, as the accused was a prominent public figure
incriminate/ɪnˈkrɪmɪneɪt/v.使负罪，连累They were afraid of answering the questions and incriminating themselves
prosecute/ˈprɑːsɪkjuːt/v.起诉The attorney who will prosecute the case says he cannot reveal how much money is involved
denounce/dɪˈnaʊns/v.谴责，痛斥denounce violence / denounce a policy
lawsuit/ˈlɔːsuːt/n.诉讼file a lawsuit / win a lawsuit
coequal/koˈikwəl/adj.同等的he elevated Brazil to the legal status of a kingdom coequal with Portugal
decree/dɪˈkriː/n.法令The decree imposed strict censorship of the media

Reference 📚

  • 《TOEFL iBT - 词以类记》

entry.title: TOEFL｜Vocab Politics
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Politics 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
faction/ˈfækʃən/n.派系/派系斗争rival factions within the administration / a party divided by faction and intrigue
factious/ˈfækʃəs/adj.导致分裂的/派系的The political party is currently dealing with factious disagreements
partisan/ˈpɑːrtɪzn/n.偏袒的Someone who is partisan strongly supports a particular person or cause, often without thinking carefully about the matter / He is clearly too partisan to be a referee
board/bɔːrd/n.委员会The Scottish tourist board / The board of directors is meeting to discuss the company’s future
Senate/ˈsɛnɪt/n.参议院The Senate will vote on the healthcare bill next week
Congress/ˈkɒŋɡrɪs/n.国会Congress is in session to discuss the new tax law
diplomacy/dɪˈploʊməsi/n.外交His sudden plunge into the field of international diplomacy is a major surprise
confederate/kənˈfɛdərɪt/n.同盟者/共犯The rebels found confederates in the neighboring country
league/liːɡ/n.联盟Several countries have formed a league to combat climate change
affiliate/əˈfɪlieɪt/n.分支机构The World Chess Federation has affiliates in around 120 countries.
unconventional/ʌnkənˈvɛnʃənl/adj.非传统的His unconventional approach to politics won him many followers
dictatorial/ˌdɪktəˈtɔːrɪəl/adj.独裁的The dictator’s dictatorial policies led to widespread unrest
domestic/dəˈmɛstɪk/adj.国内的Domestic issues were at the forefront of the election
potent/ˈpoʊtnt/adj.强有力的Something that is potent is very effective and powerful / The medication is potent, so only take the recommended dosage
authoritative/əˈθɔːrɪtətɪv/adj.权威性的the most authoritative book on the subject
centralized/ˈsɛntrəˌlaɪzd/adj.中央集权的The government is centralized and has offices in the capital
authority/əˈθɔːrɪti/n.当局This provided a pretext for the authorities to cancel the elections
democracy/dɪˈmɑːkrəsi/n.民主The country transitioned from a monarchy to a democracy
petition/pəˈtɪʃən/n.请愿They started a petition to change the local parking rules
territory/ˈtɛrɪtɔːri/n.领土，领地The government denies that any of its territory is under rebel control
nationality/ˌnæʃəˈnælɪti/n.国籍Her nationality is German, but she speaks many languages
kingdom/ˈkɪŋdəm/n.王国The Kingdom of Denmark is a constitutional monarchy
realm/rɛlm/n.领域 / 王国In the realm of physics, his research is ground-breaking / Defence of the realm is crucial
regime/ˈreɪˈʒiːm/n.政体/统治方式the collapse of the Fascist regime at the end of the war
sovereignty/ˈsɒvərɪnti/n.主权，统治权The country fought for sovereignty and independence
autonomy/ɔːˈtɑːnəmi/n.自治权The region was granted autonomy but is still part of the country
commission/kəˈmɪʃən/n.委员会The commission was set up to investigate the incident
committee/kəˈmɪti/n.委员会The committee will review the proposal before making a decision.
election/ɪˈlɛkʃən/n.选举The presidential election is held every four years
ballot/ˈbælət/n.选票The voters cast their ballots at the local polling station
ideology/ˌaɪdɪˈɒlədʒi/n.意识形态His political ideology is grounded in social justice
parade/pəˈreɪd/n.游行，阅兵式The town held a parade to celebrate the holiday / A military parade marched slowly and solemnly down Pennsylvania Avenue
govern/ˈɡʌvərn/v.统治，管理The governor will govern the state for a term of four years
confer/kənˈfɜːr/v.商讨The president will confer with his advisors before making a decision
entitle/ɪnˈtaɪtl/v.赋予权利The new law entitles all citizens to healthcare
exploit/ɪkˈsplɔɪt/v.利用，剥削The company was accused of exploiting its workers
maneuver/məˈnuːvər/n./v.策略/演习diplomatic manoeuvres （外交策略） / The army practiced a defensive maneuver
emigrate/ˈɛmɪɡreɪt/v.移民He emigrated to Belgium
immigrate/ˈɪmɪɡreɪt/v.迁入，移民He immigrated to the United States when he was young
enslave/ɪnˈsleɪv/v.奴役To enslave someone means to make them into a slave / The invading army enslaved the local population
impel/ɪmˈpɛl/v.驱使His desire for knowledge impelled him to study
oust/aʊst/v.罢免/革职He was ousted as chairman / The board voted to oust the CEO
impeachɪmˈpiːtʃv.弹劾to impeach the president
banish/ˈbænɪʃ/v.放逐，驱逐If someone or something is banished from a place or area of activity, they are sent away from it and prevented from entering it / John was banished from England
deport/dɪˈpɔːrt/v.驱逐出境The illegal immigrants were deported back to their home country
exile/ˈeksaɪl/n./v.被流放to be/live in exile
reign/reɪn/n./v.统治，主权Queen Victoria reigned over Britain for over 60 years / in/during the reign of Charles II
abdicate/ˈæbdɪkeɪt/v.退位If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen / The king was forced to abdicate the throne
administration/ədˌmɪnɪˈstreɪʃən/n.行政机关/管理The school administration is responsible for setting academic policy / the day-to-day administration of a company
institute/ˈɪnstɪtjuːt/v./n.设立/机构The government decided to institute new regulations / a research institute
amendment/əˈmɛndmənt/n.修改/ 修正案The 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote
colonize/ˈkɒlənaɪz/v.殖民，开拓European powers colonized many parts of Africa in the 19th century
monarchy/ˈmɒnərki/n.君主制The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy
republican/rɪˈpʌblɪkən/adj./n.共和党人The Republican candidate won the election
anarchism/ˈænərkɪzəm/n.无政府主义Anarchism proposes a society free from governmental control
doctrine/ˈdɒktrɪn/n.教义，主义the Marxist doctrine of perpetual revolution
municipal/mjuːˈnɪsɪpəl/adj.市政的The municipal authorities gave the go-ahead for the march / municipal elections
strike/straɪk/n./v.罢工The workers went on strike for better wages
scandal/ˈskændl/n.丑闻The political scandal led to the president’s resignation
welfare/ˈwɛlfɛər/n.福利Welfare programs aim to support those in financial need
bureaucracy/bjʊˈrɒkrəsi/n.官僚制度State bureaucracies can tend to stifle enterprise and initiative (国家官僚体制会压抑人的进取心和积极性)
designation/ˌdɛzɪɡˈneɪʃən/n.指定，名称The district is under consideration for designation as a conservation area
reactionary/riˈækʃəneri/n.反动的/ 保守的A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country / The Portuguese revolutionaries framed a liberal constitution for the kingdom, but they were conservative or reactionary in relation to Brazil
abrogate/ˈæbrəɡeɪt/v.废除Soon it became clear that the Portuguese parliament intended to set the clock back by abrogating all the liberties and concessions won by Brazil since 1808
position/pəˈzɪʃ(ə)n/n.看法/立场My parents always took the position that early nights meant healthy children / to take a moderate position on most of the key issues
strategic importance/strəˈtiːdʒɪk/n.战略重要性The choice of Memphis by Egypt’s first kings reflects the site’s strategic importance
opportune location/ˌɑːpərˈtuːn/adj.恰好的/适当的the apex of the Nile River delta was a politically opportune location for the state’s administrative center
preoccupation/priˌɑːkjuˈpeɪʃn/n.关注/首要任务Access to, and control of, trade routes between Egypt and the Near East seems to have been a preoccupation of Egypt’s rulers during the period of state formation

entry.title: TOEFL｜Vocab Botany
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Botany 🚀

entry.title: TOEFL｜Vocab Archaeology
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Archaeology 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
archaeology/ˌɑːrkiˈɑːlədʒi/n.考古学She studied archaeology at university
archaeological/ɑːrkiəˈlɑːdʒɪk(ə)l/adj.考古学的The evolution of the symbolism is reflected in the archaeological record first of all by the increasing complexity of the tokens themselves

antique/ænˈtiːk/n.古董，古物He is fond of collecting antiques
artisan/ˈɑːrtɪzən/n.工匠Before 1815 manufacturing in the United States had been done in homes or shops by skilled artisans
antiquity/ænˈtɪkwəti/n.古代（尤指古希腊和古罗马）/ 古物The statue was brought to Rome in antiquity (这座雕像是古时运到罗马的) / The museum contains the remains of Chinese antiquity (博物馆藏有中国古代的遗物)

excavation/ˌekskəˈveɪʃn/n.挖掘，发掘They conducted an excavation at the historical site
Neolithic/ˌniːəˈlɪθɪk/adj.新石器时代的They found Neolithic pottery at the site
Mesolithic/ˌmezəˈlɪθɪk/adj.中石器时代的The archaeologists discovered Mesolithic tools in the excavation
Paleolithic/ˌpeɪlioʊˈlɪθɪk/adj.旧石器时代的The cave contains Paleolithic drawings
preliterate/priːˈlɪtərət/adj文字出现以前的Researchers demonstrated that preliterate people created a system of accounting
chronological/ˌkrɒnəˈlɒdʒɪkl/adj.按年代顺序的They arranged the artifacts in chronological order
archaic/ɑːrˈkeɪɪk/adj.古老的，古代的Archaic means extremely old or extremely old-fashioned / They discovered an archaic burial ground
ascend/əˈsend/v.上升，攀升The team ascended to the top of the archaeological site
primitive/ˈprɪmɪtɪv/adj.原始的，早期的They found primitive tools in the cave
remnant/ˈremnənt/n.残余，遗迹They found remnants of an ancient civilization
porcelain/ˈpɔːrsəlɪn/n.瓷，瓷器She collects Chinese porcelain
pharaoh/ˈferoʊ/n.法老The pyramids were built by the ancient pharaohs of Egypt
manuscript/ˈmæn.juː.skript/n.手稿，原稿They discovered an ancient manuscript in the cave
script/skript/n.文字系统the earliest evidence of writing is the cuneiform Sumerian script
cuneiform/ˈkjuːnɪfɔːrm/n.楔形文字the earliest evidence of writing is the cuneiform Sumerian script on the clay tablets of ancient Mesopotamia
hieroglyphic/haɪərəˈɡlɪfɪk/n.象形文字Two of the three alphabets are ancient Egyptian scripts that stop being used: the **hieroglyphic **and the demotic
pictograph/ˈpɪktəɡræf/n.象形文字The signs marked on clay tablets likewise evolved from simple wedges, circles, ovals, and triangles based on the plain tokens to pictographs derived from the complex tokens
unequivocal/ˌʌnɪˈkwɪvək(ə)l/adj.明确的Coprolites yield unequivocal evidence about the dietary habits of dinosaurs / an unequivocal rejection

owl/aʊl/n.猫头鹰-
personnel/ˌpɝː.səˈnel/n.员工personnel department (人事部门) / military personnel (军事人员)
physiology/ˌfɪz.iˈɑː.lə.dʒi/n.生理学study physiology
picky/ˈpɪk.i/adj.挑剔的Some people are very picky about who they choose to share their lives with
picturesque/ˌpɪk.tʃəˈresk/adj.如画的picturesque landscape
pointed/ˈpɔɪn.tɪd/adj.尖锐的pointed comment (尖锐的)
potter/ˈpɑː.t̬ɚ/n./v.陶艺家/闲逛potter around (闲逛)
predominate/prɪˈdɑː.mə.neɪt/v.主导Women predominated in the audience
principal/ˈprɪn.sə.pəl/n./adj.校长/首要的The principal reason for this omission is lack of time
proprietor/prəˈpraɪ.ə.t̬ɚ/n.业主，所有者The proprietor of a hotel, shop, newspaper, or other business is the person who owns it
quiescent/kwiˈes.ənt/adj.静止的Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive
rally/ˈræl.i/n./v.集会/召集rally support
relay/ˈriː.leɪ/n./v.接力赛/转达relay message (转达消息)
repertoire/ˈrep.ər.twɑːr/n.全部节目actor’s repertoire
shrimp/ʃrɪmp/n.虾shrimp cocktail (虾鸡尾酒)
starch/stɑːrtʃ/n./v.淀粉There’s too much starch in your diet
sweeping/ˈswiː.pɪŋ/adj.全面的sweeping reforms/changes
swift/swɪft/adj./n.快速的swift response
tendon/ˈten.dən/n.腱Achilles tendon (跟腱)
trilogy/ˈtrɪl.ə.dʒi/n.三部曲science fiction trilogy
twinkling/ˈtwɪŋ.kəl.ɪŋ/n./adj.闪烁的in the twinkling of an eye
utility/juːˈtɪl.ə.t̬i/n./adj.公用事业utility bill (水电费) / public utilities such as gas, electricity and phones

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 21 & 22
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Word List 21 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
aggregate/ˈæɡrɪɡət/n./v.总数/聚集aggregate demand/investment/turnover (总需求/投资/成交量)
alternative/ɔːlˈtɜːrnətɪv/n./adj.替代的/选择New ways to treat arthritis may provide an alternative to painkillers (治疗关节炎的新方法可能会提供一种止痛药的替代品)
ambience/ˈæmbiəns/n.气氛/环境the relaxed ambience of the city (这座城市轻松的氛围)
anecdotal/ˌænɪkˈdoʊtl/adj.轶事的Anecdotal evidence is based on individual accounts, rather than on reliable research or statistics, and so may not be valid
apartment/əˈpɑːrtmənt/n.公寓a two-bedroom apartment (两室一厅的公寓)
arthritis/ɑːrˈθraɪtɪs/n.关节炎arthritis treatment (关节炎治疗)
authentic/ɔːˈθɛntɪk/adj.真实的/真正的authentic cuisine (地道的美食)
banner/ˈbænər/n.横幅a banner ad (横幅广告)
botany/ˈboʊtni/n.植物学a botany professor (植物学教授)
calcium/ˈkælsiəm/n.钙calcium supplement (钙补充剂)
chaste/tʃeɪst/adj.贞洁的lead a chaste life (过着贞洁的生活)
closet/ˈklɑːzɪt/n.衣柜walk-in closet (步入式衣柜)
concise/kənˈsaɪs/adj.简洁的Sam’s text is concise and informative (文字简洁、内容丰富)
confederacy/kənˈfɛdərəsi/n.联盟A confederacy is a union of states or people who are trying to achieve the same thing (同盟/联盟)
contagious/kənˈteɪdʒəs/adj.有传染性的contagious disease (传染病)
convention/kənˈvɛnʃən/n.会议/公约Geneva Convention (日内瓦公约)
deplete/dɪˈpliːt/v.耗尽deplete natural resources (耗尽自然资源)
emblem/ˈɛmbləm/n.徽章/象征national emblem (国徽) / The eagle was an emblem of strength and courage (鹰是力量和勇气的象征)
funding/ˈfʌndɪŋ/n.资金funding for research (研究资金)
garb/ɡɑːrb/n.服装prison garb 囚服
halt/hɔːlt/v./n.停止come to a halt (停下来)
incursion/ɪnˈkɜːrʒən/n.入侵resist the incursion (抵抗入侵)
inn/ɪn/n.小旅馆stay at an inn (在客栈住宿)
internship/ˈɪntɚˌʃɪp/n.实习take up an internship (开始实习)
journalism/ˈdʒɝːnəˌlɪzəm/n.新闻业I’ve made some useful contacts in journalism (我在新闻界结交了一些有用的人)
linger/ˈlɪŋɡɚ/v.逗留linger in one’s mind (留在某人心中)
livestock/ˈlaɪvˌstɑːk/n.家畜livestock farming (畜牧业) / Livestock farm (养殖场/饲养场)
methane/ˈmeθeɪn/n.甲烷，沼气methane emissions (甲烷排放)
mine/maɪn/v./n.矿coal mine (煤矿)
moth/mɔːθ/n.蛾moth balls (防蛀球)
onslaught/ˈɔːnˌslɔːt/n.攻击/猛攻The press launched another vicious onslaught on the president （新闻界对这位总统进行了新一轮的恶毒抨击）
outlying/ˈaʊtˌlaɪɪŋ/adj.偏远的outlying districts (偏远地区)
patronizing/ˈpætrəˌnaɪzɪŋ/adj.高人一等的patronizing attitude (居高临下的态度)
pictorial/pɪkˈtɔːrɪəl/adj.图片的pictorial representation (插图表示)
platelike/ˈpleɪtˌlaɪk/adj.板状的platelike structure (板状结构)
premature/ˌpriːməˈtʃʊr/adj.过早的premature birth (早产) / premature death(早逝/非自然死亡)
proliferate/prəˈlɪfəˌreɪt/v.激增articles on the subject has proliferated over the last year (过去一年以来，论及这一问题的文章大量涌现)
resin/ˈrezɪn/n.树脂pine resin (松树脂)
revere/rɪˈvɪr/v.崇敬revere as a god (尊为神) / The Chinese revered corn as a gift from heaven (中国人将谷物奉为天赐礼物)
sparse/spɑːrs/adj.稀疏的sparse population (稀疏的人口)
spectacle/ˈspektəkl/n.眼镜/奇观The sunset was a stunning spectacle (夕阳西斜，异常壮观)
strap/stræp/n./v.带子a watch with a leather strap (皮表带的手表)
tariff/ˈtærɪf/n.关税impose a tariff (征收关税)
thesis/ˈθiːsɪs/n.论文doctoral thesis (博士论文)
welfare/ˈwelfer/n.幸福/福利welfare state (福利国家) / We are concerned about the child’s welfare （我们关注那个孩子的福祉）

Word List 22 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
algebra/ˈældʒɪbrə/n.代数学algebra class (代数课)
cascade/kæˈskeɪd/n./v.瀑布/倾泻/连续cascade effect (级联效应)
chart/ʧɑːrt/n./v.图表/记录The exhibition charts the history of the palace (展览记载了这座王宫的历史)
circulation/ˌsɜːr.kjʊˈleɪ.ʃən/n.循环/发行数量blood circulation (血液循环)
complement/ˈkɑːmplɪmənt/n./v.补充complement each other (互补)
conductor/kənˈdʌktər/n.导体/指挥train conductor (火车司机) / Graphite is a highly efficient conductor of electricity (石墨是一种高效的电导体)
congress/ˈkɑːŋɡrɪs/n.国会the U.S. Congress (美国国会)
coupon/ˈkuːpɑːn/n.优惠券discount coupon (折扣券)
critique/krɪˈtiːk/n./v.评论literary critique (文学评论)
crown/kraʊn/n./v.王冠/加冕crown a king (加冕为王)
defect/‘di:feɪkt/n./v.缺陷He was born with a hearing defect (他天生听力就有缺陷)
dehydrated/diːˈhaɪdreɪtɪd/adj.脱水的dehydrated food (脱水食品)
distinctive/dɪˈstɪŋktɪv/adj.独特的the distinctive odour of chlorine (氯气的特殊气味)
drawbacks/ˈdrɔːbæk/n.缺点weigh the pros and cons/drawbacks (权衡利弊)
evolve/ɪˈvɑːlv/v.逐步发展/进化evolve from (由…进化而来)
expel/ɪkˈspel/v.驱逐expel from school (从学校开除)
extract/ɪkˈstrækt/ , /ˈekstrækt/n./v.提取extract information (提取信息)
fatal/ˈfet̬.əl/adj.致命的a fatal error (致命错误)
finalize/ˈfaɪ.nəl.aɪz/v.定稿/完成finalize a deal (完成一项交易)
flask/flæsk/n.瓶，烧瓶a flask of coffee (一瓶咖啡)
fluctuate/ˈflʌktʃueɪt/v.波动prices fluctuate (价格波动)
frugal/ˈfruː.ɡəl/adj.节俭的a frugal lifestyle (节俭的生活方式)
genetics/dʒɪˈnetɪks/n.遗传学study of genetics (遗传学的研究)
germinate/ˈdʒɝː.mə.neɪt/v.发芽/开始发展seeds germinate (种子发芽)
glorify/ˈɡlɔː.rə.faɪ/v.美化glorify the past (美化过去)
hawk/hɔːk/n./v.鹰/叫卖hawk goods (叫卖商品)
humanity/hjuːˈmæn.ə.t̬i/n.人类crimes against humanity (反人类罪)
jot/dʒɑːt/v./n.草草记下jot down notes (草草记下笔记)
lasting/ˈlæs.tɪŋ/adj.持久的lasting impression (持久的印象)
litter/ˈlɪt̬.ɚ/n./v.垃圾don’t litter (不乱丢垃圾)
machinery/məˈʃiː.nər.i/n.机器，机械heavy machinery (重型机械)
magnitude/ˈmæɡ.nə.tuːd/n.量级of great magnitude (重大的)
methanol/ˈmeθ.ə.nɑːl/n.甲醇methanol fuel (甲醇燃料)
microorganism/ˌmaɪ.kroʊˈɔːr.ɡə.nɪ.zəm/n.微生物harmful microorganism (有害微生物)
nightmare/ˈnaɪtˌmer/n.恶梦have a nightmare (做噩梦)
pertinent/ˈpɝː.t̬ən.ənt/adj.相关的pertinent information/questions (相关信息/问题)
plunge/plʌndʒ/v./n.突然跌落At least 50 people died when a bus plunged into a river （一辆公共汽车冲进了河里，至少有50人死亡）
reference/ˈref.ər.əns/n./v.提及/参考She made no reference to her illness (她没有谈论她的病) / reference book (参考书)
repute/rɪˈpjuːt/n./v.声望She is a writer of international repute (她是一位享有国际声誉的作家)
ridge/rɪdʒ/n.山脊ridge of a hill (山脊)
rodeo/ˈroʊ.di.oʊ/n.牛仔竞技表演attend a rodeo (参加牛仔竞技表演)
satellite/ˈsæt̬.əl.aɪt/n.卫星launch a satellite (发射一颗卫星)
satire/ˈsæt̬.aɪr/n.讽刺political satire (政治讽刺)
scarf/skɑːrf/n./v.围巾wear a scarf (戴围巾)
somewhat/ˈsʌm.wɑːt/adv.有点somewhat larger (稍大一些)
soothe/suːð/v.安抚/缓和soothe the pain (缓解疼痛)
sophisticated/səˈfɪs.tɪ.keɪ.t̬ɪd/adj.复杂的/精密的sophisticated technology (先进的技术)
spin/spɪn/v./n.旋转/纺织spin a web (结网)
spinet/ˈspɪn.ɪt/n.小型立式钢琴play the spinet (弹小型立式钢琴)
suite/swiːt/n.套房a suite of rooms/offices (一套房间/办公套房) / a hotel/private/honeymoon suite (旅馆/私人/蜜月套房)
trivial/ˈtrɪv.i.əl/adj.琐碎的trivial matter (琐事)
turn-out/ˈtɝːn.aʊt/n./v.出席人数high turn-out (高出席率)
turnpike/ˈtɝːn.paɪk/n.收费公路drive on the turnpike (在收费公路上驾驶)
unaided/ʌnˈeɪ.dɪd/adj.无助的/独立的unaided effort (独立的努力)
unsubstantiated/ˌʌn.səbˈstæn.ʃi.eɪ.t̬ɪd/adj.无事实依据的an unsubstantiated claim/rumour, etc (未经证实的说法/传言)
warp/wɔːrp/v./n.扭曲/变形Left out in the heat of the sun, tapes easily warp or get stuck in their cases (放在太阳底下暴晒后，磁带容易翘曲变形或卡带)

Reference 📚

  • 《TOEFL词汇（45天突破版）》
  • https://www.collinsdictionary.com/
  • https://openai.com/blog/chatgpt

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 19 & 20
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Word List 19 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
abrupt/əˈbrʌpt/adj.突然的abrupt change (突然的变化)
accessory/əkˈsesəri/n.配件，附件fashion accessories (时尚配饰)
antibiotic/ˌæntibaɪˈɒtɪk/n.抗生素antibiotic therapy (抗生素疗法)
bond/bɒnd/n./v.纽带/债券form a bond (形成纽带)
cafeteria/ˌkæfɪˈtiəriə/n.自助餐厅school cafeteria (学校餐厅)
compromise/ˈkɒmprəmaɪz/n./v.和解reach a compromise (达成妥协)
constricted/kənˈstrɪktɪd/adj.受限制的Film-makers of the time were constricted by the censors (那时的电影制作人受到了审查官的限制)
discern/dɪˈsɜːrn/v.辨别，识别discern the truth (辨别真相)
documentary/ˌdɒkjʊˈmentəri/n.纪录片watch a documentary (看纪录片)
domestic/dəˈmestɪk/adj.国内的domestic flight (国内航班)
draft/drɑːft/n./v.草稿/起草draft a proposal (起草提案)
elective/ɪˈlɛktɪv/n./adj.选修课elective course (选修课)
enlightment/ɪnˈlaɪtənmənt/n.启蒙the Age of Enlightenment (启蒙时代)
equitable/ˈekwɪtəbəl/adj.公正的equitable treatment (公平待遇)
estate/ɪˈsteɪt/n.财产/庄园real estate (房地产)
fresco/ˈfrɛskoʊ/n.壁画Sistine Chapel frescoes (西斯廷礼拜堂的壁画)
frivolity/frɪˈvɒlɪti/n.轻浮acts of frivolity (轻浮的行为)
hazel/ˈheɪzl/n./adj.榛树/淡褐色的hazel eyes (淡褐色的眼睛)
herbivore/ˈhɜːrbɪvɔːr/n.草食动物herbivorous dinosaur (草食恐龙)
huddle/ˈhʌdəl/v./n.聚在一起huddle together (挤在一起)
hue/hjuː/n.色彩various hues of blue (各种蓝色的色调)
inflation/ɪnˈfleɪʃən/n.通货膨胀high inflation rate (高通胀率)
instructor/ɪnˈstrʌktər/n.指导者/讲师fitness instructor (健身教练)
leather/ˈlɛðər/n.皮革leather jacket (皮革夹克)
liberate/ˈlɪbəreɪt/v.解放liberate a city (解放一座城市)
mansion/ˈmænʃən/n.大厦/豪宅mansion house (大厦)
mottled/ˈmɑːtld/adj.斑驳的mottled skin (斑驳的皮肤)
noted/ˈnoʊtɪd/adj.著名的a noted historian (知名的历史学家)
oceanographer/ˌoʊʃəˈnɑːɡrəfər/n.海洋学家-
paralyze(paralyse)/ˈpærəlaɪz/v.使瘫痪paralyze the economy (使经济瘫痪)
parasite/ˈpærəsaɪt/n.寄生虫intestinal parasites (肠道寄生虫)
prescribe/prɪˈskraɪb/v.开处方prescribe medication (开药方)
regenerate/rɪˈdʒɛnəˌreɪt/v.使复兴/重建The government will continue to try to regenerate inner-city areas (政府将继续努力重建市区内部)
resilience/rɪˈzɪliəns/n.适应力，恢复力emotional resilience (情绪恢复力)
rhyme/raɪm/n./v.韵脚rhyme scheme (韵脚方案)
shade/ʃeɪd/n./v.阴凉处Let’s sit in the shade for a while (咱们在阴凉处坐一会儿吧)
sow/soʊ/v./n.播种sow the seeds (播种)
substitute/ˈsʌbstɪˌtut/v./n.替代substitute teacher (代课教师)
sustained/səˈsteɪnd/adj.持续的sustained effort (持续的努力)
tundra/ˈtʌndrə/n.冻原Tundra is flat land with very little vegetation (苔原是平坦的土地，植被稀少)
vessel/ˈvɛsl/n.船/血管blood vessel (血管)
voracious/vəˈreɪʃəs/adj.贪婪的voracious reader (酷爱阅读的人)

Word List 20 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
abound/əˈbaʊnd/v.充满The lakes abound with fish (这些湖泊盛产鱼)
amble/ˈæmbəl/v./n.漫步，闲逛amble around (四处闲逛)
beam/biːm/n./v.光束beam of light (光束)
bellow/ˈbɛloʊ/v./n.吼叫/风箱bellow with rage (愤怒地咆哮)
cape/keɪp/n.海角Cape of Good Hope (好望角)
caterpillar/ˈkætərpɪlər/n.毛毛虫The caterpillar will eventually metamorphose into a butterfly (毛毛虫最终将蜕变成一只蝴蝶)
characteristic/ˌkærɪktəˈrɪstɪk/n./adj.特征/典型的Genes determine the characteristics of every living thing (基因决定每个生物的特征) / Windmills are a characteristic feature of the Mallorcan landscape (风车是马略卡岛风光的一个典型的特色)
colonize/ˈkɑːləˌnaɪz/v.殖民/开拓colonize a planet (开拓一颗行星)
delay/dɪˈleɪ/v./n.推迟delay a project (推迟一个项目)
eclecticism/ɪˈklɛktɪˌsɪzəm/n.折衷主义-
elasticity/ɪˌlæstɪˈsɪti/n.弹性the skin’s elasticity (皮肤弹性)
embellish/ɪmˈbɛlɪʃ/v.装饰Ivy leaves embellish the front of the dresser (长春藤树叶装饰着梳妆台的正面)
endangered/ɪnˈdeɪndʒərd/adj.濒临灭绝的endangered species (濒危物种)
evacuation/ɪˌvækjuˈeɪʃən/n.撤离emergency evacuation (紧急撤离)
exploit/ɪkˈsplɔɪt/v./n.利用/剥削to prevent exploitation (阻止剥削)
facade/fəˈsɑːd/n.（建筑物的）正面Squalor and poverty lay behind the city’s glittering façade (表面的繁华掩盖了这座城市的肮脏和贫穷)
fracture/ˈfræktʃər/v./n.断裂/骨折bone fracture (骨折)
guideline/ˈɡaɪdˌlaɪn/n.指导方针follow the guidelines (遵循指导方针)
horn/hɔːrn/n.角horn of a rhinoceros (犀牛角)
hurl/hɜːrl/v.猛掷Simon caught the grenade and hurled it back (西蒙接住手榴弹，把它掷了回去)

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配

porcelain/ˈpɔːrsəlɪn/n.瓷器porcelain vases
postpone/poʊˈspoʊn/v.延期，推迟postpone a meeting (推迟会议)
presidency/ˈprɛzɪdənsi/n.总统职位the current holder of the EU presidency

terminus/ˈtɝːmɪnəs/n.终点站reach the terminus
territory/ˈtɛrɪtɔːri/n.领土，领地disputed territory
topsoil/ˈtɑːpˌsɔɪl/n.表层土壤topsoil contains few of the ingredients needed for long-term successful farming (表层土壤几只含有少量长期成功耕作所必需的成分)
transit/ˈtrænsɪt/n./v.运输/穿越goods damaged in transit (在运输中损坏的货物) / transit through a country (穿越一个国家)

Word List 10 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
abort/əˈbɔːrt/v.中止，终止abort the mission (中止任务)

cluster/ˈklʌstər/n.群，簇，串a cluster of grapes (一串葡萄)
debris/ˈdeɪbriː/n.碎片，残骸debris of the plane (飞机残骸)
destined/ˈdɛstɪnd/adj.注定的be destined to fail (注定失败)
elementary/ˌɛlɪˈmɛntəri/adj.基本的，初级的elementary school (小学)
engraving/ɪnˈɡreɪvɪŋ/n.雕刻，版画This type of engraving requires a delicate touch (这种雕刻要求手法轻巧)
entitle/ɪnˈtaɪtl/v.给予权利They are entitled to first class travel (他们有权享受头等舱旅行)
farce/fɑːrs/n.闹剧，笑剧turn into a farce (变成闹剧)
fulfill/fʊlˈfɪl/v.实现，完成fulfill a promise (履行承诺)
gospel/ˈɡɒspəl/n.福音书/真理gospel truth (真理)
hamper/ˈhæmpər/v.妨碍，阻挠hamper the progress (阻碍进展)
hygiene/ˈhaɪdʒiːn/n.卫生，卫生学personal hygiene (个人卫生)
ideology/ˌaɪdɪˈɒlədʒi/n.意识形态political ideology (政治理念)
infrared/ɪnfrəˈred/adj.红外线的infrared radiation (红外线辐射)
junction/ˈdʒʌŋkʃən/n.路口，交叉点at the junction (在交叉路口)
laureate/ˈlɔːriət/n.获奖人Nobel laureate (诺贝尔奖得主)
mammoth/ˈmæməθ/adj./n.巨大的/猛犸象mammoth task (艰巨的任务)
mania/ˈmeɪniə/n.狂热football mania (足球狂热)
muggy/ˈmʌɡi/adj.闷热潮湿的a muggy summer day (闷热潮湿的夏天)
outbreak/ˈaʊtbreɪk/n.爆发，暴动outbreak of war (战争爆发)
overload/ˌoʊvərˈloʊd/v./n.超载，过载an overloaded truck (一辆超载的卡车)
partial/ˈpɑːrʃl/adj.部分的/偏袒的be partial to someone (偏袒某人)
populate/ˈpɒpjuleɪt/v.居住于，生息populate the area (在该地区居住)
prevailing/prɪˈveɪlɪŋ/adj.盛行的prevailing wind (盛行风)
prohibitively/prəˈhɪbɪtɪvli/adv.(价格)高昂的prohibitively expensive (价格过于高昂)
proofread/ˈpruːfriːd/v.校对proofread a manuscript (校对手稿)
quota/ˈkwoʊtə/n.配额，限额immigration quota (移民配额)
rampant/ˈræmpənt/adj.泛滥的，猖獗的Inflation is rampant (通货膨胀肆虐)
recital/rɪˈsaɪtl/n.独奏会piano recital (钢琴独奏会)
reckless/ˈrɛkləs/adj.鲁莽的reckless driving (鲁莽驾驶)
restoration/ˌrɛstəˈreɪʃən/n.恢复，修复building restoration (建筑修复)
rodent/ˈroʊdnt/n.啮齿动物Mickey Mouse starts as an ugly, little rodent (米老鼠开始是又丑又小的噬齿动物)
scuba/ˈskuːbə/n.水肺潜水scuba diving (水肺潜水)
sewerage/ˈsuːərɪdʒ/n.下水道系统city sewerage system (城市下水道系统)
silt/sɪlt/n.淤泥，淤沙silt deposition (淤沙沉积)
stripe/straɪp/n.条纹，军衔a tiger’s stripes (老虎的条纹)
tension/ˈtɛnʃən/n.紧张，压力tension in the air (空气中的紧张感)
treadmill/ˈtrɛdmɪl/n.跑步机run on a treadmill (在跑步机上跑步)
tributary/ˈtrɪbjutɛri/n.支流a tributary of the Amazon (亚马逊的支流)
undertaking/ˌʌndərˈteɪkɪŋ/n.任务，工作a difficult undertaking (困难的任务)
unparalleled/ʌnˈpærəleɪld/adj.无比的，无双的unparalleled beauty (无比的美)
vigilance/ˈvɪdʒɪləns/n.警惕，警觉maintain vigilance (保持警惕)
wane/weɪn/v.衰退，减少Her popularity has been on the wane for some time (她的人气不断下降) / wane of the moon (月亏)

Reference 📚

  • 《TOEFL词汇（45天突破版）》
  • https://www.collinsdictionary.com/
  • https://openai.com/blog/chatgpt

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
acidity/əˈsɪdɪti/n.酸度acidity of vinegar (醋的酸度)
acting/ˈæktɪŋ/adj./n.演戏，代理的acting manager (代理经理)， acting skills (表演技巧)

aquifer/ˈækwɪfɚ/n.含水土层underground aquifer (地下含水层)

buckle/ˈbʌkl/n./v.扣子，扣紧buckle your belt (扣紧你的皮带)
cardiac/ˈkɑːrdiæk/adj./n.心脏的，心脏病患者cardiac arrest (心脏停搏)， cardiac patient (心脏病患者)

chagrin/ʃəˈɡrɪn/n./v.失望，懊恼to her chagrin (使她失望的是)

Word List 8 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
administer/ədˈmɪnɪstər/v.管理，执行，给予administer medication (给予药物)
astute/əˈstuːt/adj.敏锐的，狡猾的an astute observer (敏锐的观察者)
bud/bʌd/n./v.芽，发芽bud of a plant (植物的芽)
canal/kəˈnæl/n.运河，人工水道the Suez Canal (苏伊士运河)
chill/tʃɪl/n./v./adj.寒冷，冷淡，冷静a chill in the air (空气中的寒冷)
cuneiform/kjuːˈniːɪfɔːrm/n./adj.楔形的，楔形文字cuneiform writing (楔形文字写作)
democrat/ˈdɛməkræt/n.民主主义者，民主党人a democrat politician (民主党政治家)

engaging/ɪnˈɡeɪdʒɪŋ/adj.吸引人的，迷人的an engaging story (吸引人的故事)
enrollment/ɪnˈroʊlmənt/n.登记，入学，入伍school enrollment (学校入学登记)
film/fɪlm/n./v.影片，薄膜，拍摄film a movie (拍摄一部电影)
fitness/ˈfɪtnəs/n.健康，适合physical fitness (身体健康)
flamboyant/flæmˈbɔɪənt/adj.艳丽的，浮夸的flamboyant style (浮夸的风格)
folklore/ˈfoʊklɔːr/n.民间传说，民间风俗study of folklore (民俗学研究)
generalization/ˌdʒɛnərəlɪˈzeɪʃən/n.概括，归纳make a generalization (做出一个概括)
incessantly/ɪnˈsɛsəntli/adv.不停地，连续不断地rain incessantly (连续不断地下雨)
larva/ˈlɑːrvə/n.幼虫larva of a butterfly (蝴蝶的幼虫)
lease/liːs/n./v.租赁，租约lease a car (租赁一辆车)
magnificent/mæɡˈnɪfɪsənt/adj.宏伟的，壮丽的a magnificent view (壮丽的景色)
meteorologist/ˌmiːtɪəˈrɒlədʒɪst/n.气象学家a meteorologist predicts weather (气象学家预测天气)
omit/oʊˈmɪt/v.省略，遗漏omit a word (省略一个词)
orientation/ˌɔːriːənˈteɪʃən/n.方向，定位，取向orientation session (定向会议)
pore/pɔːr/n.毛孔，细孔pores on the skin (皮肤上的毛孔)
portrait/ˈpɔːrtrɪt/n.肖像，画像portrait painting (肖像画)
prerequisites/priːˈrɛkwɪzɪts/n.先决条件，必备条件prerequisites for admission (入学的先决条件)
prolific/prəˈlɪfɪk/adj.多产的，丰富的a prolific writer (多产的作家)
punctual/ˈpʌŋktʃuəl/adj.准时的，守时的be punctual for meetings (会议准时)
rust/rʌst/n./v.锈，
saturated/ˈsætʃəreɪtɪd/adj.饱和的，充满的saturated solution (饱和溶液)
screen/skriːn/n./v.屏幕，筛选screen a movie (放映一部电影)
skyscraper/ˈskaɪˌskreɪpər/n.高楼大厦skyscraper city (摩天大楼的城市)

strand/strænd/n./v.细线， strands of hair (头发丝); 搁浅， strand on an island (搁浅在岛上)

tuition/tuːˈɪʃən/n.学费tuition fees (学费)

warehouse/ˈwɛərhaʊs/n.仓库warehouse storage (仓库存储)

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 5 & 6
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Word List 5 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
ailment/ˈeɪlmənt/n.疾病An ailment is an illness, especially one that is not very serious / Many people suffer from some sort of chronic ailment
assimilate/əˈsɪmɪleɪt/v.吸收/融入This technique brings life to instruction and eases assimilation of knowledge / It took time for the immigrant to assimilate into the new culture
chubby/ˈʧʌbi/adj.圆胖的A chubby person is somewhat fat / The baby has chubby cheeks
courageous/kəˈreɪdʒəs/adj.勇敢的Firefighters are courageous people who risk their lives to save others / The children were very courageous
credential/krɪˈdɛnʃəl/n.资历/资格证书Someone’s credentials are their previous achievements, training, and general background, which indicate that they are qualified to do something
detergent/dɪˈtɜrdʒənt/n.清洁剂Please add some detergent to the washing machine
excavation/ˌɛkskəˈveɪʃən/n.挖掘The excavation of the ancient city took several years
evaluate/ɪˈvæljueɪt/v.评估We need to evaluate how well the policy is working
evacuate/ɪˈvækjueɪt/v.撤离Children were evacuated from London to escape the bombing
facilitate/fəˈsɪlɪteɪt/v.促进Computers facilitate the processing of large amounts of information
foremost/ˈfɔrmoʊst/adj.最重要的The foremost thing or person in a group is the most important or best / Health should be our foremost concern
frenzy/ˈfrɛnzi/n.狂热The crowd was whipped into a frenzy during the concert
friction/ˈfrɪkʃən/n.摩擦/冲突There was a lot of friction between the two colleagues
imprint/ˈɪmprɪnt/n.印记，痕迹If something leaves an imprint on a place or on your mind, it has a strong and lasting effect on it / As I arrived, the shimmering skyline of domes and minarets was imprinted on my memory
induce/ɪnˈduːs/v.引起/导致Doctors said surgery could induce a heart attack
inert/ɪˈnɜːrt/adj.惰性的/不活跃的The gas is inert and will not react with the other substances in the mixture / Inert gases like neon and argon have eight electrons in their outer shell
infection/ɪnˈfɛkʃən/n.感染It is important to clean wounds properly to avoid infection / The likelihood of infection is minimal
intuitive/ɪnˈtjuːɪtɪv/adj.直觉的If you have an intuitive idea or feeling about something, you feel that it is true although you have no evidence or proof of it / He had an intuitive sense of what the reader wanted
isolated/ˈaɪsəˌleɪtɪd/adj.偏僻的/孤立的An isolated place is a long way away from large towns and is difficult to reach / If you feel isolated, you feel lonely and without friends or help
jelly/ˈʤɛli/n.果冻She made a delicious dessert using strawberry jelly
jolt/ʤoʊlt/v.颠簸/震惊If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently / The sudden jolt of the train woke up all the passengers / The plane landed with a jolt
lament/ləˈmɛnt/v.哀悼If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it / Ken began to lament the death of his only son
lithosphere/ˈlɪθoʊˌsfɪr/n.岩石圈The lithosphere is the rigid outer layer of the Earth
opposed/əˈpoʊzd/adj.反对的I am utterly opposed to any form of terrorism
overtime/ˈoʊvərˌtaɪm/n.加班He had to work overtime to finish the project on time
photodissociation/ˌfoʊtoʊˌdɪsoʊsiˈeɪʃən/n.光解作用Photodissociation is the breaking of a chemical bond caused by the absorption of light
pigeon/ˈpɪʤən/n.鸽子The pigeon is a common bird in many cities around the world
poetry/ˈpoʊətri/n.诗歌Poetry is a form of literature that uses aesthetic and rhythmic qualities of language to evoke emotions
propose/prəˈpoʊz/v.提议He proposed a new plan to increase sales
reactor/riˈæktoʊr/n.反应堆A nuclear reactor is a device used to initiate and control a sustained nuclear chain reaction
recession/rɪˈsɛʃən/n.经济衰退During a recession, there is a significant decline in economic activity across the economy
reliable/rɪˈlaɪəbl/adj.可靠的People or things that are reliable can be trusted to work well or to behave in the way that you want them to
replenish/rɪˈplɛnɪʃ/v.补充If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again / to replenish food and water supplies
scurry/ˈskʌri/v.急赶When people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened / The attack began, sending residents scurrying for cover
sensible/ˈsɛnsɪbl/adj.明智的It is sensible to save money for the future / The former option would be much more sensible
sluggish/ˈslʌɡɪʃ/adj.缓慢的The computer became sluggish after the update / Circulation is much more sluggish in the feet than in the hands
squash/skwɒʃ/v.压扁Be careful not to squash the fruit when you pack them.
subsequent/ˈsʌbsɪkwənt/adj.随后的The subsequent events were even more surprising / Subsequent events confirmed our doubts
substantiate/səbˈstænʃieɪt/v.证实He provided evidence to substantiate his claims
suburb/ˈsʌbɜːrb/n.郊区He lives in a suburb which is very peaceful
vague/veɪɡ/adj.模糊的The instructions were vague and difficult to follow
watercourse/ˈwɔːtərkɔːrs/n.水道The watercourse is essential for draining the rainwater away from the town

Word List 6 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
agreeable/əˈɡriːəbl/adj.令人愉快的If something is agreeable, it is pleasant and you enjoy it / The weather today is very agreeable for a picnic
allegiance/əˈliːdʒəns/n.忠诚They swore their allegiance to the U.S. and received their naturalization papers
angular/ˈæŋɡjələr/adj.有角的He had an angular face with prominent cheekbones
architect/ˈɑːrkɪtɛkt/n.建筑师The architect designed a modern building
cabin/ˈkæbɪn/n.小木屋We stayed in a cozy cabin in the woods
carp/kɑːrp/n.鲤鱼The pond is filled with carp
celestial/səˈlɛstʃəl/adj.天空的The celestial bodies include stars, planets, and moons
colonial/kəˈloʊniəl/adj.殖民地的，殖民的The country gained independence after years of colonial rule
comparable/ˈkɒmpərəbl/adj.可比的Farmers were supposed to get an income comparable to that of townspeople
complementary/ˌkɒmplɪˈmɛntəri/adj.互补的，补充的The two colors are complementary to each other.
cornerstone/ˈkɔːrnərstoʊn/n.奠基石The cornerstone of a successful business is a strong work ethic.
crow/kroʊ/n.乌鸦A crow cawed from a tree branch.
digression/dɪˈɡrɛʃən/n.离题The professor made several digressions during his lecture.
eccentric/ɪkˈsɛntrɪk/adj./n.古怪的，异常的 / 古怪的人He is an eccentric artist with a unique style.
eligible/ˈɛlɪdʒəbl/adj.合格的Only those over 18 years old are eligible to vote.
flagellum/fləˈdʒɛləm/n.鞭毛Some bacteria use a flagellum for movement.
fungi/ˈfʌndʒaɪ/n.真菌Mushrooms and yeasts are types of fungi.
improvise/ˈɪmprəvaɪz/v.即兴创作The musician forgot his sheet music and had to improvise.
inconspicuous/ˌɪnkənˈspɪkjuəs/adj.不显眼的，不引人注目的The spy wore inconspicuous clothing to avoid detection.
journal/ˈdʒɜːrnəl/n.日记，杂志She writes her thoughts and experiences in her journal every night.
lush/lʌʃ/adj.青翠的，丰富的The landscape was lush with greenery after the rain.
nominee/nɒˈmiːni/n.被提名人The nominee for best actor was thrilled to be recognized.
palate/ˈpælɪt/n.上颚，味觉The dish had a unique combination of flavors that pleased my palate.
quilt/kwɪlt/n.被子She made a beautiful quilt with a variety of colorful fabrics.
rancher/ˈræntʃər/n.牧场主The rancher took care of hundreds of cattle on his land.
reddish/ˈrɛdɪʃ/adj.带红色的The sunset cast a reddish hue on the landscape.
resign/rɪˈzaɪn/v.辞职The manager decided to resign after working for 10 years.
rupture/ˈrʌptʃər/n./v.断裂，破裂The rupture in the dam caused a massive flood.
sheath/ʃiːθ/n.鞘，外壳The knife is stored in a leather sheath.
shelter/ˈʃɛltər/n./v.避难所，庇护The travelers found shelter from the rain in a cave.
spherical/ˈsfɛrɪkəl/adj.球形的The Earth is not a perfect sphere but is slightly spherical.
tally/ˈtæli/n./v.计数，符合The final tally of votes showed a close race.

vacant/ˈveɪkənt/adj.空的，未占用的The house has been vacant for months.

entry.content:

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配

heading/ˈhɛdɪŋ/n.标题chapter headings

mammal/ˈmæməl/n.哺乳动物marine mammals

nomadic/noʊˈmædɪk/adj.游牧的nomadic lifestyle

pathology/pəˈθɒlədʒi/n.病理学Pathology is the study of the way diseases and illnesses develop
plaster/ˈplɑːstər/v./n.抹石膏The ceiling he had just plastered fell in and knocked him off his ladder
quench/kwɛnʧ/v.熄灭He stopped to quench his thirst at a stream
renew/rɪˈnjuː/v.更新renew a subscription
ripen/ˈraɪpən/v.(使)成熟I’m waiting for the apples to ripen

suspension/səˈspɛnʃən/n.悬挂suspension from school
therapy/ˈθɛrəpi/n.治疗physical therapy
tile/taɪl/n./v.瓦片/瓷砖ceramic floor tiles / a fine building, with a neat little porch and ornamental tiles on the roof
unadorned/ʌnəˈdɔːrned/adj.无装饰的The walls were plain and unadorned
vigorous/ˈvɪgərəs/adj.精力旺盛的Vigorous physical activities involve using a lot of energy, usually to do short and repeated actions / A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm

Word List 4 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
analogy/əˈnælədʒi/n.类比，比喻make an analogy

appraisal/əˈpreɪzəl/n.评估/ 评价performance appraisal / a calm appraisal of the situation
artifact(artefacts)/ˈɑːrtɪfækt/n.文物religious artifact
assure/əˈʃʊr/v.确保assure someone of something
attire/əˈtaɪər/n./v.穿着，服装Your attire is the clothes you are wearing / dressed in formal evening attire / All were in their night attire
catalyst/ˈkætəlɪst/n.催化剂/促进因素catalyst for change
cohesion/koʊˈhiːʒən/n.凝聚力The source of Roman obsession with unity and cohesion may well have lain in the pattern of Rome’s early development
combustible/kəmˈbʌstəbl/adj.可燃的combustible materials / combustible fumes / combustible gas
counterpart/ˈkaʊntərpɑːrt/n.对应的人或物The Secretary of State and his Russian counterpart met to try to nail down the elusive accord

documentation/ˌdɒkjʊmənˈteɪʃən/n.文件Documentation consists of documents which provide proof or evidence of something, or are a record of something

expose/ɪkˈspoʊz/v.曝光he story of how the press helped expose the truth about the Nixon administration
figurative/ˈfɪɡjərətɪv/adj.比喻的/形象（艺术）figurative language / figurative painting
forage/ˈfɔːrɪdʒ/v./n.寻找They were forced to forage for clothing and fuel / Pull yourself together, and come with me and forage
haunt/hɔːnt/v./n.萦绕在心头The memory of that day still haunts me
homogeneous/ˌhoʊməˈdʒiːniəs/adj.同种的/均匀的homogeneous mixture
heterogenous/ˌhetərˈɑdʒənəs/adj.不均匀混合heterogenous mixture
hurricane/ˈhɜːrɪkən/n.飓风At the same time, extreme weather events like Category 5 hurricanes are becoming more frequent
intoxication/ɪnˌtɒksɪˈkeɪʃən/n.醉酒intoxication is the state of being drunk / She felt a sense of euphoria and relaxation after a few sips of the potent drink, signaling the onset of intoxication
maintenance/ˈmeɪntənəns/n.保养，维修vehicle maintenance / maintenance cost
memo/ˈmɛmoʊ/n.备忘录/简报to write/send/circulate a memo
mold(mould)/moʊld/n./v.模具/霉菌mold into shape
neoclassical/ˌniːoʊˈklæsɪkəl/adj.新古典主义的neoclassical architecture
ornament/ˈɔːrnəmənt/n./v.装饰品a china/glass ornament
oyster/ˈɔɪstər/n.牡蛎oyster shell
paddle/ˈpædl/n./v.桨/划桨the skills you will use to paddle the canoe
perception/pərˈsɛpʃən/n.感知/认识perception of reality / Perception is not something that is hardwired into the brain
pretentious/prɪˈtɛnʃəs/adj.矫揉造作的/自命不凡的If you say that someone or something is pretentious, you mean that they try to seem important or significant, but you do not think that they are / She had a habit of using pretentious language to make herself seem more sophisticated
proceed/prəˈsid/v.继续进行proceed with caution / Work is proceeding slowly
puncture/ˈpʌŋktʃər/v./n.穿刺puncture a tire
rural/ˈrʊrəl/adj.农村的rural area / It was a delightful rural scene
rustic/ˈrʌstɪk/adj.乡村的an old cottage full of rustic charm / Nick opens the door to a rustic cabin
sculpt/skʌlpt/v.雕刻a display of animals sculpted in ice / An artist sculpted a full-size replica of her head
sledding/ˈslɛdɪŋ/n.滑雪We got home and went sledding on the small hill in our back garden
sleigh/sleɪ/n.雪橇A sleigh is a vehicle which can slide over snow / Sleighs are usually pulled by horses
spontaneous/spɒnˈteɪniəs/adj.自发的/自然的Many people spontaneously stood up and cheered / spontaneous reaction
sticky/ˈstɪki/adj.黏的The plant exudes a sticky fluid
superficial/ˌsuːpərˈfɪʃəl/adj.肤浅的The book shows only a superficial understanding of the historical context
synthetic/sɪnˈθɛtɪk/adj.合成的，人造的Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones
venom/ˈvɛnəm/n.毒液/恶毒Tarantula venom is weaker than that of a honeybee
veto/ˈviːtoʊ/n./v.否决权/否决The British government used its veto to block the proposal
vicinity/vɪˈsɪnɪti/n.附近in the vicinity of

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 1 & 2
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Word List 1 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
acronym/ˈækrənɪm/n.首字母缩略词NASA is an acronym for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration
acute/əˈkjuːt/adj.严重的/急性的The war has aggravated an acute economic crisis / acute appendicitis
aggression/əˈɡrɛʃən/n.好斗情绪/侵略The research shows that computer games may cause aggression / the threat of massive military aggression
artistic/ɑːrˈtɪstɪk/adj.艺术的She’s the artistic type / She comes from a very artistic family
awareness/əˈwɛərnəs/n.认知raise awareness / an awareness of the importance of eating a healthy diet
brochure/ˈbroʊʃər/n.手册Our brochure is printed on environmentally-friendly paper
chimpanzee/ˌtʃɪmpænˈziː/n.黑猩猩You can’t hurt a chimpanzee
conductivity/kənˌdʌktˈɪvɪti/n.导电/热性Copper wire was used because of its great conductivity
congestion/kənˈdʒɛstʃən/n.堵塞traffic congestion
crevice/ˈkrɛvɪs/n.裂缝a huge boulder with rare ferns growing in every crevice
deficiency/dɪˈfɪʃənsi/n.不足/缺陷vitamin deficiency
devotion/dɪˈvoʊʃən/n.奉献/热爱Her devotion to the job left her with very little free time
discharge/dɪsˈtʃɑːrdʒ/v.释放The factory was fined for discharging chemicals into the rive
dispute/dɪˈspjuːt/v./n.争论a dispute between the two countries about the border
diverse/daɪˈvɜːrs/adj.多种多样的people from diverse cultures
doctrine/ˈdɒktrɪn/n.学说The doctrine of surplus value is the cornerstone of Marx’s economic theory
expire/ɪkˈspaɪər/v.到期/失效He had lived illegally in the United States after his visitor’s visa expired
fare/fɛər/v., n.交通费用bus/taxi fares
foul/faʊl/adj.肮脏的/犯规foul air/breath / foul play
juvenile/ˈdʒuːvənaɪl/adj.（动物）幼年的juvenile animals
log/lɒɡ/n.原木a thick piece of wood that is cut from or has fallen from a tree
maritime/ˈmærɪtaɪm/adj.海事的/海洋的a maritime museum
mat/mæt/n., v.垫子yoga mat
obstruct/əbˈstrʌkt/v.阻碍The authorities are obstructing a United Nations investigation
overcharge/ˌoʊvərˈtʃɑːrdʒ/v., n.过高收费overcharge for a service
pollen/ˈpɑːlən/n.花粉Seeds and pollen are spread by the wind
predominant/prɪˈdɒmɪnənt/adj.明显的/占优势的a predominant feature (显著特征)
prevalent/ˈprevələnt/adj.盛行的prevalent disease / This condition is more prevalent in women than in me
protagonist/prəˈtæɡənɪst/n.主人公/倡导者the protagonist of J. D. Salinger’s novel “The Catcher in the Rye.”
rehabilitate/ˌriːəˈbɪlɪteɪt/v.恢复健康Considerable efforts have been made to rehabilitate patients who have suffered in this way
sapphire/ˈsæfaɪər/n.蓝宝石sapphire ring
scatter/ˈskætər/v.分散/撒She tore the rose apart and scattered the petals over the grave
sensual/ˈsensʃuəl/adj.感官的The book brings a sensual pleasure
shellfish/ˈʃɛlˌfɪʃ/n.水生有壳动物Fish and shellfish are the specialties
shuttle/ˈʃʌtəl/n./v.来往于两地之间的航班a shuttle service between London and Edinburgh
sodium/ˈsoʊdiəm/n.钠Sodium and sulphur are highly corrosive
spice/spaɪs/n./v.香料/调料herbs and spices / common spices such as ginger and cinnamon
stylistic/staɪˈlɪstɪk/adj.风格的/文体的Wilde is also a friend of Yeats, but Yeats’ poetry has indeed undergone importantand notable stylistic changes
surplus/ˈsɝː.pləs/n.过剩food surpluses / Surplus grain is being sold for export
syllable/ˈsɪləbəl/n.音节‘Potato’ is stressed on the second syllable
temporary/ˈtem.pər.er.i/adj.临时的I’m looking for some temporary work
tow/toʊ/v./n.拖车They threatened to tow away my car
unearth/ʌnˈɝːθ/v.挖掘Researchers have unearthed documents from the 1600s / to unearth buried treasures
varnish/ˈvɑːrnɪʃ/v./n.上清漆/清漆varnish a table / The varnish takes a few hours to harden

Word List 2 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
accord/əˈkɔːrd/v./n.一致 / 条约be in accord with / The two sides signed a peace accord last July
additive/ˈædɪtɪv/n./adj.添加物food additives / additive-free orange juice
affection/əˈfɛkʃən/n.喜爱Your affections are your feelings of love or fondness for someone / Children need lots of love and affection
alternately/ɔːlˈtɜːrnətli/adv.轮流地The two methods can be used alternately
coil/kɔɪl/v./n.线圈/盘绕a coil of wire / Mist coiled around the tops of the hills
composer/kəmˈpoʊzər/n.作曲家music by Strauss, Mozart, Beethoven, and other great composers
dairy/ˈdeəri/n.奶制的dairy products
deceive/dɪˈsiːv/v.欺骗He has deceived and disillusioned us all
forestall/fɔːrˈstɔːl/v.预先阻止forestall a crisis / Large numbers of police were in the square to forestall any demonstrations
fume/fjuːm/n./v.冒烟/气体She sat in the car, silently fuming at the traffic jam / car exhaust fumes
igneous/ˈɪgniəs/adj.火成的having solidifed from lava or magma / igneous rock
immutable/ɪˈmjuːtəbl/adj.不变的immutable laws of nature / the eternal and immutable principles of right and wrong
impetus/ˈɪmpɪtəs/n.促进因素His articles provided the main impetus for change
intriguing/ɪnˈtriːgɪŋ/adj.引人入胜的If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange / This intriguing book is both thoughtful and informative
justify/ˈdʒʌstɪfaɪ/v.证明…有理No argument can justify a war
legislative/ˈlɛdʒɪsleɪtɪv/adj.立法的legislative powers / Today’s hearing was just the first step in the legislative process
legitimate/lɪˈdʒɪtɪmət/adj.合法的the legitimate government of the country / Is his business strictly legitimate ?
literacy/ˈlɪtərəsi/n.读写能力Literacy is the ability to read and write / Many adults have problems with literacy and numeracy
locomotion/ˌloʊkəˈmoʊʃn/n.移动Locomotion is the ability to move and the act of moving from one place to another / means of locomotion
longitude/ˈlɔːndʒɪtuːd/n.经度the longitude of a place
marked/mɑːrkt/adj.明显的There has been a marked increase in crimes against property
modulate/ˈmɒdjʊleɪt/v.调节/改变He carefully modulated his voice / These chemicals modulate the effect of potassium
motto/ˈmɒtoʊ/n.座右铭The school’s motto is: ‘Duty, Honour, Country’
paramount/ˈpærəmaʊnt/adj.首要的/至高无上的This matter is of paramount importance (此事至关重要) / China’s paramount leader
pendant/ˈpɛndənt/n.吊坠，垂饰The pendant was set with pearls surrounding an emerald

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 45

moisture/ˈmɔɪstʃər/n.水分，湿气skin moisture (皮肤水分)
municipal/mjuːˈnɪsɪpəl/adj.市政的，地方自治的municipal government（市政府）/ municipal elections（市政选举）
nauseous/ˈnɔːsiəs/adj.恶心的，令人作呕的She felt dizzy and nauseous（她觉得头晕、恶心）/ a nauseous smell（令人作呕的气味）
oppose/əˈpoʊz/v.反对oppose a plan (反对一个计划)
orbital/ˈɔːrbɪtl/adj.轨道的an orbital path（天体运行轨道）
orchestra/ˈɔːrkɪstrə/n.管弦乐队，交响乐团symphony orchestra (交响乐团)
pensive/ˈpɛnsɪv/adj.沉思的；忧伤的to look pensive（神情忧伤）/ She stared pensively out of the window at the rain（她忧郁地凝望着窗外的雨）
peripheral/pəˈrɪfərəl/adj.次要的/边缘的peripheral vision (周边视觉) / peripheral device (外围设备) / peripheral information (辅助信息)
pound/paʊnd/n./v.英镑a pound of apples (一磅苹果)
prestige/prɛˈstiːʒ/n.声望gain prestige (获得声望)
relic/ˈrɛlɪk/n.遗迹the last remaining relic（仅存的遗迹）/ a relic of the past (过去的遗迹)
resort/rɪˈzɔːrt/n./v.度假胜地/诉诸a holiday resort (度假胜地) / resort to violence (诉诸暴力)
sauce/sɔːs/n./v.酱汁/给…加调料apple sauce (苹果酱) / sauce the salad (给沙拉加调料)
scout/skaʊt/n./v.侦察a scout troop（侦察队）/ scout for information（寻找信息）/ to join the Scouts（参加童子军）
seclusion/sɪˈkluːʒən/n.孤立the seclusion and peace of the island（岛上的幽僻宁静）/ live in seclusion (独居)
supplement/ˈsʌplɪmənt/n./v.补充，添加dietary supplement（饮食补充）/ supplement income (补充收入)
transmitter/trænsˈmɪtər/n.发射器radio transmitter（无线电发射器）
tropic/ˈtrɒpɪk/n.热带Tropic of Cancer（北回归线）/ the Tropic of Capricorn（南回归线）
vent/vɛnt/n./v.通风口/宣泄air vent（通风口）/ vent frustration（宣泄挫败感）
volume/ˈvɒljuːm/n.容量/册volume of a cylinder（圆柱体的容量）/ the first volume of the series（系列的第一册）
zinc/zɪŋk/n.锌zinc plate (锌板)

entry.title: TOEFL｜Word List 43 & 44
entry.content:
TOEFL Vocabulary (feat.ChatGPT)

Word List 43 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
abbreviate/əˈbriː.vi.eɪt/v.缩写abbreviate a word（缩写一个词）
aerial/ˈeə.ri.əl/adj./n.天线的/空中的aerial view（鸟瞰视角）/ aerial photograph（航空照片）
annex/ˈænɛks/v./n.强占/附加Germany annexed Austria in 1938（1938年德国吞并了奥地利）/ annex a document (附加一份文件)
blanket/ˈblæŋkɪt/n./v.毯子/覆盖blanket with snow（被雪覆盖）
clarify/ˈklær.ə.faɪ/v.澄清，阐明clarify the meaning（阐明含义）
confession/kənˈfeʃ.ən/n.坦白/忏悔make a confession（作出坦白/忏悔）
consciously/ˈkɑːn.ʃəs.li/adv.有意识地Consciously or unconsciously, you made a choice（不管是有意还是无意，你已作出了选择）
cosmis/ˈkɒzmɪk/adj.宇宙的the cosmic laws（宇宙法则）
crisscross/ˈkrɪs.krɔːs/v., n., adj.纵横交错crisscross pattern（纵横交错的图案）
damp/dæmp/adj., n., v.潮湿的damp clothes（潮湿的衣服）
definitive/dɪˈfɪn.ɪ.t̬ɪv/adj.确定的/权威的definitive guide（权威指南） / a definitive answer（一个确定的回答）
evolution/ˌiː.vəˈluː.ʃən/n.进化，演变theory of evolution（进化论）
expedition/ˌek.spəˈdɪʃ.ən/n.远征，探险to plan/lead/go on an expedition to the North Pole（计划/带队/去北极探险）
fault/fɔːlt/n., v.错误It’s not my fault（这不是我的错）
flock/flɑːk/n., v.一群a flock of birds（一群鸟）
girder/ˈɡɝː.dɚ/n.主梁steel girder（钢梁）
hieroglyph/ˈhaɪ.rəˌɡlɪf/n.象形文字hieroglyph script（象形文字脚本）
incubate/ˈɪŋ.kjə.beɪt/v.孵化，培养incubate eggs（孵化鸡蛋）
ironical/aɪˈrɑːn.ɪ.kəl/adj.讽刺的ironical comment（讽刺的评论）
irresistible/ˌɪr.ɪˈzɪs.tə.bəl/adj.不可抗拒的irresistible charm (不可抗拒的魅力)
microbe/ˈmaɪ.kroʊb/n.微生物Deepsea microbes（深海微生物）/ harmful microbes（有害的微生物）
monument/ˈmɑː.nə.mənt/n.纪念碑war monument（战争纪念碑）
nerve-cell/ˈnɝːv sel/n.神经细胞healthy nerve cells（健康的神经细胞）
oratorio/ˌɔːrəˈtɔːrioʊ/n.清唱剧Handel’s oratorios（亨德尔的清唱剧）
pivot/ˈpɪv.ət/n.枢轴pivot point（枢轴点）
plump/plʌmp/adj., v., adv.丰满的a plump face（饱满的面庞） / the berries were plump and sweet（这些浆果饱满而甘甜）
polygon/ˈpɑː.lɪ.ɡɑːn/n.多边形regular polygon（规则多边形）
ponderous/ˈpɑːn.dər.əs/adj.笨重的，冗长乏味的ponderous speech（冗长乏味的演讲）
predecessor/ˈpriː.dəˌses.ɚ/n.前任，前辈his predecessor（他的前任）
rational/ˈræʃənl/adj.理性的rational thinking（理性思考）
readily/ˈrɛdɪli/adv.欣然地；轻易地All ingredients are readily available from your local store.（所有的原料都可以方便地从你当地的商店买到）
rejuvenate/rɪˈdʒuːvɪneɪt/v.使恢复活力protect and rejuvenate local operas（保护和振兴地方戏曲）/ great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation（中华民族伟大复兴）
resident/ˈrɛzɪdənt/n.居民resident of the city（城市的居民）
scrape/skreɪp/v., n.刮；擦伤scrape the surface （刮表面）
shuffle/ˈʃʌfl/v., n.洗牌/拖着脚走shuffle the cards (洗牌) / He shuffled across the kitchen.（他莫伊拉拖着脚走过了厨房）
simmer/ˈsɪmər/v.用文火炖simmer the sauce（用文火慢炖调味汁） / simmer with resentment（满肚怨火）
specialized/ˈspɛʃəˌlaɪzd/adj.专业的；专门的specialized skills (专门技能)
spur/spɝː/n., v.鼓励；刺激I was spurred into action by the letter（那封信激励我行动起来）
substance/ˈsʌbstəns/n.物质chemical substance（化学物质）
tenant/ˈtɛnənt/n.租户tenant of the apartment（公寓的租户）
tentacle/ˈtɛntəkl/n.触手octopus tentacles（章鱼触手）
tenuous/ˈtɛnjuəs/adj.纤细的/脆弱的a tenuous argument（站不住脚的论点）/ He holds a rather tenuous position in history（他在历史上的地位不高）
ultraviolet/ʌltrəˈvaɪəlɪt/adj., n.紫外线的ultraviolet rays（紫外线）
variation/ˌveəriˈeɪʃən/n.变化/变种variation in temperature（温度变化） / slight variations in pressure（微小的压力变化）

Word List 44 🚀

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配
abiding/əˈbaɪdɪŋ/adj.持久的He has a genuine and abiding love of the craft（他对这门手艺有着一种发自内心和持久不变的热爱）
aloof/əˈluːf/adj.冷淡的，疏远的He used to be aloof（他以前很孤僻）/ The Emperor kept himself aloof from the people（皇帝对人民漠不关心）
anatomy/əˈnætəmi/n.解剖学study of anatomy (解剖学的研究)
antique/ænˈtiːk/n., adj.古董a genuine antique（一件真古董）/ an antique shop（古玩店）/ an antique dealer（古董商）
applicable/ˈæplɪkəbl/adj.可适用的applicable laws (适用的法律)
auditorium/ˌɔːdɪˈtɔːriəm/n.礼堂，观众席school auditorium (学校礼堂)
barn/bɑːrn/n.谷仓a hay barn (干草仓库)
cling/klɪŋ/v.粘贴，紧抓cling to hope (紧紧抓住希望)
coax/koʊks/v.哄骗coax someone into doing (哄骗某人做某事)
commentary/ˈkɒməntəri/n.现场解说sports commentary (体育实况解说)
cramped/kræmpt/adj.狭小的，拥挤的cramped conditions (拥挤的环境)
crippling/ˈkrɪplɪŋ/adj.导致瘫痪的，严重的Those are crippling diseases（导致残疾的疾病）/ crippling debt (严重的债务)
dissolve/dɪˈzɒlv/v.溶解dissolve sugar in water (在水中溶解糖)
dorsal/ˈdɔːrsl/adj.背部的dorsal fin (背鳍)
elusive/ɪˈluːsɪv/adj.难以捉摸的，/难以实现的elusive dream (难以实现的梦想)
epitomize/ɪˈpɪtəmaɪz/v.是…的典型These movies seem to epitomize the 1950s（这些影片似乎是20世纪50年代的缩影）/ epitomize the spirit of an era (代表一个时代的精神)
exhilarating/ɪgˈzɪləˌreɪtɪŋ/adj.令人兴奋的My first parachute jump was an exhilarating experience（我第一次跳伞的经历很令人激动）
fortuitous/fɔːrˈtjuːɪtəs/adj.偶然的a fortuitous encounter (一次偶然的相遇)
illusion/ɪˈluːʒən/n.幻觉，错觉optical illusion (光学错觉)
inspect/ɪnˈspɛkt/v.检查inspect the facilities (检查设施)
motive/ˈmoʊtɪv/n.动机I’m suspicious of his motives（我怀疑他的动机）
mural/ˈmjʊrəl/n.壁画a mural of San Francisco Bay（一幅旧金山湾壁画）
niche/niːʃ/n.商机spotted a niche in the market（发现商机）
nostalgia/nɒˈstældʒə/n.怀旧feel a sense of nostalgia (感到怀旧)
organism/ˈɔːrɡənɪzəm/n.有机体，生物a complex organism (复杂的有机体)
perpendicular/ˌpɜːr.pənˈdɪk.jə.lər/adj.垂直的perpendicular to the ground (垂直于地面)
prestigious/prɛˈstɪdʒəs/adj.有声望的，有威望的a prestigious university (一所有威望的大学)
pyramid/ˈpɪr.ə.mɪd/n.金字塔the pyramids of Egypt (埃及的金字塔)
quaint/kweɪnt/adj.古雅的，别致的a quaint little village (一座古雅的小村庄) / a small, quaint town（一座古朴的小镇）
recollection/ˌrɛkəˈlɛkʃən/n.回忆，记忆a vague recollection (模糊的回忆)
rhinoceros/raɪˈnɑːsərəs/n.犀牛a herd of rhinoceros (一群犀牛)
rivalry/ˈraɪ.vəl.ri/n.竞争business rivalry (商业竞争)
senator/ˈsɛnətər/n.参议员a U.S. Senator (美国参议员)
spinning/ˈspɪnɪŋ/n./v.旋转/纺纱spinning wheel (纺车)
spray/spreɪ/n./v.喷雾；喷射sea spray（海上的浪花）/ spray paint (喷漆)
squirrel/ˈskwɪrəl/n.松鼠a red squirrel (一只红松鼠)
sumptuous/ˈsʌmptʃuəs/adj.奢华的sumptuous surroundings（富丽堂皇的环境）/ a sumptuous meal (豪华的一餐)
trench/trɛntʃ/n.沟渠，战壕dig a trench (挖沟)
ultimatum/ʌlˈtɪməˌtum/n.最后通牒issue an ultimatum (发出最后通牒)
vacate/vəˈkeɪt/v.空出，撤离Guests should vacate their rooms by 10.30 a.m（旅客应在上午10:30以前腾出房间）
variable/ˈvɛriəbəl/adj./n.可变的/变量The potassium content of foodstuffs is very variable（食品中钾的含量是多变的）
withdraw/wɪðˈdrɔː/v.撤回withdraw a statement (撤回声明)

单词音标词性中文含义短语搭配

chamber/ˈtʃeɪmbər/n.室，房间chamber of commerce ）商会）/ the Senate/House chamber（参议院/众议院会议厅）

infancy/ˈɪnfənsi/n.婴儿期，初期in its infancy (处于初期)
interplay/ˌɪntərˈpleɪ/n.相互作用，交互the interplay of political, economic, social and cultural factors（政治、经济，社会和文化因素的互相影响）
limestone/ˈlaɪmstoʊn/n.石灰石limestone quarry (石灰石采矿场)

oblivious/əˈblɪviəs/adj.忘记的/未察觉的oblivious to pain（感觉不到疼痛）/ oblivious to the danger (对危险未察觉)
pasture/ˈpæstʃər/n.牧场cattle pasture (牛的牧场)
percussion/pərˈkʌʃən/n.打击乐器，冲击percussion instrument (打击乐器)
physician/fɪˈzɪʃən/n.医师，内科医生family physician (家庭医生)
portraiture/ˈpɔːrtrɪtʃər/n.画像技巧，肖像portrait painting (肖像画)
prescription/prɪˈskrɪpʃən/n.处方，规定medical prescription (医疗处方)
pretension/prɪˈtenʃən/n.虚饰/做作He spoke without pretension（他有话直说，不装相）/ without pretension (毫无矫饰)
